{{short description|Statistical technique}}
'''Multiple abstract variance analysis (MAVA)''', is a statistical technique used to estimate the proportion of variance in a [[phenotypic trait]] due to [[genetics|genetic]] and [[environment (biophysical)|environment]]al factors. It was developed by psychologist [[Raymond B. Cattell]] in order to enable the analysis of data from multiple independent sources to estimate the causes of trait variation. Cattell originally described the technique in a 1960 paper.<ref>{{Cite book |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0kPuBwAAQBAJ |title=Handbook of Multivariate Experimental Psychology |last1=Vogler |first1=George P. |last2=Fulker |first2=David W. |date=2013-11-11 |publisher=[[Springer Science & Business Media]] |isbn=9781461308935 |editor-last=Nesselroade |editor-first=John R. |editor-link=John Nesselroade |page=480 |language=en |chapter=Human Behavior Genetics |author-link2=David W. Fulker |editor-last2=Cattell |editor-first2=Raymond B. |editor-link2=Raymond B. Cattell}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cattell |first=Raymond B. |date=1960 |title=The multiple abstract variance analysis equations and solutions: For nature-nurture research on continuous variables. |journal=[[Psychological Review]] |language=en |volume=67 |issue=6 |pages=353–372 |doi=10.1037/h0043487 |pmid=13691636 |issn=1939-1471}}</ref> MAVA aims to estimate the relative genetic and environmental contributions to trait variation by comparing variances between families to those within families on the trait under study. As such, it is considered a "more systematic and comprehensive approach" than the classical [[correlation]] method of [[heritability]] estimation.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Dempsey |first1=P. J. |last2=Townsend |first2=G. C. |date=June 2001 |title=Genetic and environmental contributions to variation in human tooth size |journal=[[Heredity (journal)|Heredity]] |volume=86 |issue=6 |pages=685–693 |doi= 10.1046/j.1365-2540.2001.00878.x|pmid=11595049 |issn=0018-067X|doi-access=free }}</ref> MAVA later formed the basis of Cattell's [[16PF Questionnaire]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Wilson |first=Philip K. |date=2010-10-23 |title=The Cattell Controversy: Race, Science, and Ideology (review) |url=https://muse.jhu.edu/article/399428 |journal=[[Journal of the History of Medicine and Allied Sciences]] |language=en |volume=65 |issue=4 |pages=587–589 |issn=1468-4373|doi=10.1093/jhmas/jrq032 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> 

MAVA has been criticized for inconsistencies between some of the mathematical [[equation]]s used in the method,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Loehlin |first=John C. |author-link=John C. Loehlin |date=1965 |title=Some methodological problems in Cattell's Multiple Abstract Variance Analysis. |journal=Psychological Review |volume=72 |issue=2 |pages=156–161 |doi=10.1037/h0021706 |pmid=14282673 |issn=0033-295X}}</ref> and for introducing "...numerous new theoretical constructs
without any clear empirical basis".<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sullivan |first1=Patrick F. |author-link=Patrick F. Sullivan |last2=Eaves |first2=Lindon J. |author-link2=Lindon Eaves |date=2002 |title=Evaluation of Analyses of Univariate Discrete Twin Data |journal=[[Behavior Genetics (journal)|Behavior Genetics]] |language=en |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=221–227 |doi=10.1023/a:1016025229858 |pmid=12141783 |s2cid=37275547 |issn=0001-8244}}</ref> Critics of the method have also noted that it requires the introduction of additional parameters whenever a new type of genetic relationship is considered, which precludes a complete analysis of the causes of trait variation.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Eaves |first1=L. J. |last2=Last |first2=Krystyna |last3=Martin |first3=N. G. |author-link3=Nick Martin (scientist) |last4=Jinks |first4=J. L. |author-link4=John L. Jinks |date=May 1977 |title=A progressive approach to non-additivity and genotype-environmental covariance in the analysis of human differences |journal=[[British Journal of Mathematical and Statistical Psychology]] |language=en |volume=30 |issue=1 |pages=1–42 |doi=10.1111/j.2044-8317.1977.tb00722.x |issn=0007-1102}}</ref>
